## Appearance

Paul Irving possesses big, serious, and very dark blue eyes set within features of exquisite delicacy and refinement. Previously characterized by a mop of chestnut or brown curls, his hairstyle has since been updated to close-cropped brown locks.

_Sources: [v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P7](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0007), [v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P21](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0021), [v2 XIX Just a Happy Day P27](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0027), [v2 XXVII An Afternoon at the Stone House P29](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0029), [v2 XXVII An Afternoon at the Stone House P30](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0030), +1 more_

## Personality

Paul Irving is a fair-minded, manly child who stands out as a perfect little gentleman and voluntarily keeps himself clean. Recognized as a genius and an uncommon youth, he possesses a remarkably imaginative mind alongside flashes of uncanny insight that make it difficult to keep secrets around him.

_Sources: [v2 VIII Marilla Adopts Twins P32](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0032), [v2 VIII Marilla Adopts Twins P52](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0052), [v2 XI Facts and Fancies P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038), [v2 XVIII An Adventure on the Tory Road P3](../source/v02-c18.md#nw-v02-c18-p0003), [v2 XXIII Miss Lavendar’s Romance P36](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0036), [v2 XXVII An Afternoon at the Stone House P54](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0054)_

## History

Paul Irving was a young student who instantly formed a close bond with his teacher, [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), on her first day at the [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) schoolhouse. Imaginative by nature, he frequently shared fantastical stories about his fictional shore friends and wrote creative compositions, such as a piece describing a moonshine boat. Three years after the death of his mother, who used to sit with him until he fell asleep, Paul spoke openly with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) about his memories of her and his inner thoughts. Through [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), Paul met Miss [Lavendar](../character/lavendar-lewis.md) at [Echo Lodge](../codex/places.md#echo-lodge) and quickly formed a sweet bond of mutual understanding with her while discussing her imaginary dream-boy. When Paul's father, [Stephen Irving](../character/stephen-irving.md), arrived in town, [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) helped reunite him with Miss [Lavendar](../character/lavendar-lewis.md), leading to their wedding and leaving the local community buzzing over the romance.

_Sources: [v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P2](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0002), [v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P13](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0013), [v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P14](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0014), [v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P15](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0015), [v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P16](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0016), +409 more_

## Quotes

> "I’ve eaten enough to make anyone grow. I do hope, now that I’ve begun, I’ll keep on till I’m as tall as father. He is six feet, you know, Miss Lavendar."
>
> — Paul Irving — [v2 XXVII An Afternoon at the Stone House P24](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0024)

> "I think you would make a splendid mother. You have just the right look in your eyes . . . the look my little mother always had. I think it’s a pity you haven’t any boys of your own."
>
> — Paul Irving — [v2 XXVII An Afternoon at the Stone House P58](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0058)

> "you can’t think what has happened! Something so splendid. Father is here . . . just think of that! Father is here! Come right in. Father, this is my beautiful teacher. You know, father."
>
> — Paul Irving — [v2 XXVIII The Prince Comes Back to the Enchanted Palace P21](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0021)

> “Yes; but if dryads are foolish they must take the consequences, just as if they were real people,” said Paul gravely. “Do you know what I think about the new moon, teacher? I think it is a little golden boat full of dreams.”
>
> — Paul Irving — [v2 XIX Just a Happy Day P30](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0030)

> "He knows I won’t associate with him if he doesn’t. He is really full of wickedness, I think."
>
> — Paul Irving — [v2 XV The Beginning of Vacation P14](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0014)
